Hi Vanessa — thanks for the reminder. We're excited to see Redwood's inference flow, but I need to flag that our leadership just announced a company-wide sales kickoff and a product sprint starting next week. A number of folks who were going to attend (including Grant and two engineers from platform) are being pulled into prep.

Would you be willing to move the demo out a couple of weeks? We still want to proceed but can't commit the right stakeholders this week.

Apologies for the churn — Emma

Hi Emma — totally understood, thanks for the heads up.

We can absolutely pivot. A couple of quick options:
- Option A: Pause this week and aim for the week of Nov 23 when your sprint winds down.
- Option B: Keep the 45-min demo but narrow attendees to a product manager + one engineer so we can cover the end-to-end story and record it for the broader team.

If you prefer Option A I can send available slots and a tentative calendar hold. If you prefer Option B I can adjust the agenda to focus on the evaluation criteria Grant mentioned (latency SLA, data isolation, cost estimates).

Also attaching a short proposed agenda for your review.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz

We do want to keep Redwood in the pipeline; can we park the live demo and ask for a recorded session + one pagedocument summarizing performance/cost tradeoffs for our exec review? We'll target reconvening in early January when resourcing clears up.

Looping in product here — if Helix wants a recorded session + an exec-ready one-pager, we should prepare:
- A 10–12 minute recorded walkthrough that shows: model selection, latency numbers on an apples-to-apples workload, and how fallback routing works.
- A one-pager (PDF) with: expected cost per 1k tokens by config, SLOs by deployment mode, and the proposed timeline for a pilot kickoff in Jan.

I can draft the one-pager and Jonas can record the walkthrough. Vanessa — can you confirm the primary questions Grant/VP will want answered so we tailor the materials?
